newsitem.title: GREECE: Cost of living tops Greek consumer complaint list.
newsitem.headline: Cost of living tops Greek consumer complaint list.

text.p: The cost of living topped Greek consumers' complaints in 1996, overtaking 1995 leader OTE telecom, the president of the consumers' institute (INKA) told Reuters.
"The high cost of living accounted for 16.8 percent of total complaints in 1996," said Charalambos Kouris.
Complaints about OTE dropped to 9.05 percent in 1996 from 25.7 percent in 1995, he said.
The cost of living is a widespread problem cutting across various income groups, he said.

Asked if that meant that headline CPI inflation was not a reliable indicator of the cost of living, Kouris said there have been always suspicions that CPI inflation underestimated the true cost of living.
"The CPI is disputed and there are problems on how sampling is being done," he said. "Prices in the central market of Athens, for example, are lower than elsewhere in the city."

Greece's revised CPI-based inflation fell to 6.8 percent year-on-year from 7.3 percent in December. The revised CPI inflation uses 1994 as the base year instead of 1988 which was the base year for the previous consumer price index.

An official at the National Statistics Service (NSS) told Reuters that the revised CPI inflation came closer to depicting the true cost of living. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
